h1: Retaining Wall Repair in St. Thomas, Ontario
intro: Newer St. Thomas subdivision walls fail differently than older ones do, usually settlement or drainage problems from fill soil that wasn't compacted properly during the original build, not age.

sections.heading: Common Failure Patterns on Newer St. Thomas Walls

blocks.text: When a subdivision wall was built quickly during development, backfill compaction and drainage are the corners most often cut. That shows up a few years later as settlement, diagonal cracking, or water pooling behind the wall after rain.
On rural St. Thomas area properties, we more often see erosion at the wall base from surface water that was never properly directed away.

items: Check for bowing or leaning out of plumb
Inspect crack patterns, horizontal cracks are the most serious
Look for blocked, missing or undersized drainage outlets
Check for soil erosion or voids at the wall base

blocks.text: A repaired wall that still lacks proper drainage will fail again. Every repair we do addresses drainage before we touch the visible damage.

Minor drainage corrections run $500 to $2,000. Larger repairs involving partial rebuilding range from $3,000 to $15,000 or more. Every repair starts with a free site assessment and a detailed written quote.

sections.heading: Repairing Walls Under Warranty vs Out of Warranty

blocks.text: If your St. Thomas home is still under a builder's structural warranty, a failing retaining wall may fall under that coverage depending on cause and timeline. We can provide documentation of our assessment to support a warranty claim where applicable.
For general guidance on what failure looks like before it gets serious, see /signs-your-retaining-wall-is-failing.

sections.heading: Documenting the Repair for Future Reference

blocks.text: After completing a repair, we can provide photos and a summary of the work done, useful if you sell the home later or need it for insurance or warranty documentation.

faqs.q: My St. Thomas subdivision wall is only a few years old and already cracking. Why?
faqs.a: It's often a sign of inadequate compaction or missing drainage from the original construction. We assess the specific cause before recommending a fix.

faqs.q: Is it worth repairing a wall on a newer home, or should it be replaced?
faqs.a: We only recommend replacement when repair genuinely won't hold. Many newer-wall problems are drainage-related and fixable without a full rebuild.

faqs.q: What are the warning signs I should watch for?
faqs.a: Bowing, horizontal cracks, water pooling at the wall base, and blocked drainage outlets are the main ones. See /signs-your-retaining-wall-is-failing for the full list.

faqs.q: Do you provide a written quote before starting repair work?
faqs.a: Yes, always, with no surprise charges once work begins.

faqs.q: Could my wall repair be covered under a builder's warranty?
faqs.a: Possibly, depending on the home's age and the cause of failure. We can document our assessment findings to support a warranty claim if relevant.

faqs.q: Will I get documentation of the completed repair?
faqs.a: Yes, we can provide photos and a summary of the work, useful for future reference or if you sell the property.

faqs.q: What if the original wall installer is no longer in business?
faqs.a: That's common, and it doesn't affect our ability to assess and repair the wall. We evaluate the existing structure on its own merits and design a repair around what we find on site, regardless of who built it originally.
